title_en: Shanghai Huanxin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Faruina Technology Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: In cases of patent infringement disputes, if the prior art on which the alleged infringer bases its prior art defense is a technical solution disclosed by the alleged infringer itself or by a third party acting under its instruction in violation of express or implied confidentiality obligations, the people's court shall not support the prior art defense based on such technical solution.

full_text_en:
Shanghai HuanXin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong FaRuiNa Technology Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent

【Ruling Gist】

In a case of patent infringement, if the prior art on which the alleged infringer relies to assert a prior art defense is a technical solution disclosed by the alleged infringer himself or a third party authorized by him in violation of an express or implied confidentiality obligation, the people's court shall not support the alleged infringer's prior art defense based on such technical solution.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 1568

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shanghai HuanXin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 5C8-1, Building 15, No. 481 Guiping Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Zhao Wei, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Lou Jun, lawyer of Shanghai Junyue Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Guangdong FaRuiNa Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 2, Chang'an Zhen'an East Road, Chang'an Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Fang Jiantao, Executive Director and Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Huang Rendong, lawyer of Guangdong Junxi Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Jiangsu Shuixiang Zhouzhuang Tourism Co., Ltd. Domicile: Quanfu Road, Zhouzhuang Town, Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhu Lirong, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Bin, lawyer of Shanghai Jinmao (Kunshan) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ni Xuejing, lawyer of Shanghai Jinmao (Kunshan) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Zhenbian Network Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 205, No. 40 Fuqian West Street, Pinggu Town, Pinggu District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zuo Xiurong, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Daokuan, lawyer of Beijing Zhenbang Law Firm.

The appellant, Shanghai HuanXin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as HuanXin Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2019) Su 05 Min Chu No. 177 rendered by the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province on June 24, 2020, in relation to a dispute over infringement of utility model patent with the respondents, Guangdong FaRuiNa Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as FaRuiNa Company), Jiangsu Shuixiang Zhouzhuang Tourism Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhouzhuang Tourism Company), and Beijing Zhenbian Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenbian Company). This Court accepted the case on October 9, 2020, and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law. This Court conducted inquiries of the parties on December 3, 2020 and March 18, 2021. The agent ad litem of the appellant HuanXin Company, Lou Jun, the agent ad litem of the respondent FaRuiNa Company, Huang Rendong, the agents ad litem of the respondent Zhouzhuang Tourism Company, Zhou Bin and Ni Xuejing, and the agent ad litem of the respondent Zhenbian Company, Wang Daokuan, attended the inquiries. The trial of this case has now concluded.

HuanXin Company's grounds for appeal: To set aside the original judgment; to amend the judgment to support all of HuanXin Company's claims; and to order FaRuiNa Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Facts and reasons: (1) The court of first instance erred in finding that the alleged connecting handle product (hereinafter referred to as the alleged infringing product) used prior art, resulting in erroneous findings of fact and application of law. 1. The utility model patent with patent number 201820194071.3 and titled "A Connecting Handle Applied to an Automatic Rental Terminal System" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit) relates to a connecting handle. The alleged children's stroller rental equipment consists of two parts: the stroller body and the stroller storage equipment (stroller dock). The alleged infringing product is part of the stroller body and is not included in the stroller storage equipment (stroller dock). HuanXin Company only authorized FaRuiNa Company to manufacture the stroller storage equipment (stroller dock), not the stroller body. Therefore, the stroller storage equipment (stroller dock) delivered by FaRuiNa Company would not result in the disclosure of the technical solution used in the alleged infringing product (hereinafter referred to as the alleged infringing technical solution). 2. The court of first instance erroneously determined that the alleged infringing technical solution was disclosed because the relevant product was delivered to the carrier for transport and was thus placed on the market. FaRuiNa Company only delivered the products under the Procurement Contract to the carrier for transportation. Regardless of whether the products actually delivered to the carrier by FaRuiNa Company included the alleged infringing product, the product remained under the actual control of FaRuiNa Company or HuanXin Company, remained in the intermediate stage of manufacturing, and the relevant product had not actually entered the market circulation. Moreover, HuanXin Company only received the products delivered by FaRuiNa Company to the carrier after February 8, 2018 (later than the filing date of the patent-in-suit). (2) The technical solution of the patent-in-suit was independently developed by HuanXin Company and is unrelated to FaRuiNa Company. According to the Procurement Contract signed between HuanXin Company and FaRuiNa Company, FaRuiNa Company bore a strict confidentiality obligation regarding the children's stroller rental equipment. FaRuiNa Company obtained improper benefits through its breach of contract by disclosing the technical solution of the patent-in-suit, which substantially harmed the legitimate rights and interests of HuanXin Company and violated the principles of fairness and the contractual agreement.

FaRuiNa Company argued: (1) The alleged infringing product was designed and prototyped by FaRuiNa Company, and before the filing date of the patent-in-suit, it was delivered to HuanXin Company three times on December 16, 2017, January 25, 2018, and February 4, 2018. The delivered products all had a "slotted dock + mushroom head handle" structure. The court of first instance correctly found that the alleged infringing technical solution constituted prior art. (2) HuanXin Company argued based on Article 3 of the Procurement Contract that FaRuiNa Company bore a confidentiality obligation and that the delivered product was not disclosed before actually arriving at HuanXin Company and therefore did not constitute prior art. This claim contradicts HuanXin Company's assertion that the products actually delivered to the carrier did not include the alleged infringing product. (3) The alleged infringing technical solution was designed by FaRuiNa Company and applied to other projects of FaRuiNa Company. Because HuanXin Company valued this technology of FaRuiNa Company, it abandoned the original contract and instead purchased this technology from FaRuiNa Company, and accordingly changed the price and delivery date of the purchased products. Therefore, the alleged infringing technical solution did not fall within the content stipulated in the Procurement Contract, and FaRuiNa Company had no confidentiality obligation regarding it. (4) Before the filing date of the patent-in-suit, FaRuiNa Company had already published product images and introductions including the alleged infringing technical solution on the Xuzhi website, so the alleged infringing product used prior art. In summary, FaRuiNa Company requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

Zhenbian Company argued: Zhenbian Company lawfully purchased products from FaRuiNa Company for use in the operation of the Zhouzhuang tourism scenic area and engaged in no act of intellectual property infringement. Regardless of whether the patent-in-suit technology belonged to HuanXin Company or FaRuiNa Company, Zhenbian Company should not bear tort liability. HuanXin Company prevented Zhenbian Company from legitimate operations and filed this lawsuit; Zhenbian Company reserves the right to claim compensation. In summary, Zhenbian Company requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

Zhouzhuang Tourism Company argued: Zhouzhuang Tourism Company only provided the premises to Zhenbian Company for its operations and had no connection to the patent infringement dispute in this case. It requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

HuanXin Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, which accepted the case on January 22, 2019. HuanXin Company's claims: 1. Order Zhouzhuang Tourism Company to immediately cease infringing the patent-in-suit rights of HuanXin Company and cease using the alleged infringing product; 2. Order Zhenbian Company to immediately cease infringing the patent-in-suit rights of HuanXin Company and cease using, offering for sale, and selling the alleged infringing product; 3. Order FaRuiNa Company to immediately cease infringing the patent-in-suit rights of HuanXin Company and cease manufacturing, using, offering for sale, and selling the alleged infringing product; 4. Order Zhouzhuang Tourism Company, Zhenbian Company, and FaRuiNa Company to jointly compensate HuanXin Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 500,000 and reasonable expenses for rights protection in the amount of RMB 20,904.3; 5. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne jointly by Zhouzhuang Tourism Company, Zhenbian Company, and FaRuiNa Company. Facts and reasons: HuanXin Company is the patentee of the patent-in-suit. The alleged infringing product used in the Zhouzhuang tourism scenic area managed by Zhouzhuang Tourism Company was not manufactured by HuanXin Company and was used without HuanXin Company's consent. Furthermore, according to Zhouzhuang Tourism Company, the alleged infringing product was purchased by Zhenbian Company from FaRuiNa Company. The above actions of Zhouzhuang Tourism Company, Zhenbian Company, and FaRuiNa Company infringed HuanXin Company's patent-in-suit rights and caused significant economic losses.

Zhouzhuang Tourism Company's defense at first instance: (1) The rights holder of the alleged infringing product is Zhenbian Company; Zhouzhuang Tourism Company does not have independent standing as a defendant. (2) The stroller rental equipment at the Zhouzhuang tourism scenic area has complete authorization from design patents, utility model patents, to software development, and therefore does not constitute infringement. (3) The alleged infringing product has a lawful source and does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. In summary, Zhouzhuang Tourism Company requested that HuanXin Company's claims be dismissed.

Zhenbian Company's defense at first instance: It is the purchaser and user of the alleged infringing product, which has a lawful source. FaRuiNa Company has corresponding intellectual property rights, and Zhenbian Company had no intent to infringe.

FaRuiNa Company's defense at first instance: (1) FaRuiNa Company had manufactured and sold the alleged infringing product before the filing date of the patent-in-suit. (2) Before the filing date of the patent-in-suit, FaRuiNa Company had already sold the alleged infringing product to Beijing BaMa Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as BaMa Company) and Hangzhou Daishujie Software Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Daishujie Company), and had also delivered it to HuanXin Company; the alleged infringing product had already been placed on the market. During the trial at first instance, HuanXin Company acknowledged this fact; therefore, the alleged infringing product uses prior art. (3) The amount of RMB 500,000 in damages claimed by HuanXin Company has no legal basis. There is only one alleged infringing product in this case; even if infringement is found, the amount of RMB 500,000 is excessively high.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On February 5, 2018, HuanXin Company filed an application with the China National Intellectual Property Administration for the patent-in-suit, which was granted and published on September 4, 2018. The patent is currently in force. In this case, HuanXin Company seeks protection for claim 1 of the patent-in-suit: A connecting handle applied to an automatic rental terminal system, characterized in that: it comprises a connecting portion for connecting with a shared item, the upper end of the connecting portion is provided with a mushroom-shaped fixing portion. The fixing portion comprises an identification head and a locking neck located between the identification head and the connecting portion, the identification head is provided with an identification tag; the connecting portion is provided with a gripping portion. The specification states: The technical problem to be solved by this utility model is to provide a connecting handle applied to an automatic rental terminal system which is simple in structure and capable of achieving shared management. The detailed description states: A connecting handle applied to an automatic rental terminal system comprises a connecting portion for connecting with a shared item. The fixing portion adopts a circular mushroom head structure, which can conveniently hang the shared item into the fixing dock, allowing the shared item to slide easily within the fixing dock while ensuring firmness. The connecting portion is provided with a gripping portion, which forms a T-shape with the connecting portion for convenient gripping.

On October 22, 2018, upon application by HuanXin Company, the Shanghai Oriental Notary Public Office conducted evidence preservation notarization of the alleged infringing product at the Zhouzhuang tourism scenic area and issued Notarial Certificate (2018) Hu Dong Zheng Jing Zi No. 18456.

After comparison, the court of first instance found that the alleged infringing product possessed all the technical features of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit and fell within the scope of protection of claim 1. FaRuiNa Company did not dispute that the technical features of the alleged infringing product were identical to those of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, but argued that the technical solution of the patent-in-suit was designed and used first by itself, and raised defenses of prior use right and prior art.

Based on this, the court of first instance further found:

On November 17, 2017, Daishujie Company (Party A) and FaRuiNa Company (Party B) signed Contract No. 2017111601, stating that Party A purchased products from Party B: shared children's stroller equipment. FaRuiNa Company's delivery note stated: delivery date December 30, 2017, contract number 2017111601, product name shared children's stroller. Another delivery note stated: delivery date November 25, 2017, contract number 2017111601, product name shared children's stroller 3D printed handle (with chip).

On October 24, 2017, BaMa Company (Party A) and FaRuiNa Company (Party B) signed Procurement Contract No. 2017102401, stating that Party A purchased three units of shared stroller equipment from Party B.

On February 1, 2018, BaMa Company (Party A) and FaRuiNa Company (Party B) signed Contract for Work No. 2018012901, stating that Party B was to complete the manufacture of the mold for Party A's shared children's stroller handle and the production of the initial trial products according to Party A's design and quality requirements. The contracted product name was shared children's stroller handle, with remarks that it was equipped with an RFID sensor and QR code, and a product appearance shape. FaRuiNa Company's delivery note stated: delivery date April 4, 2018, contract number 2018012901, product name shared children's stroller accessories (handle, QR code).

On October 27, 2017, HuanXin Company (Party A, purchaser) and FaRuiNa Company (Party B, seller) signed a Procurement Contract, stating that Party A purchased the following products from Party B: 50 units of children's stroller rental equipment (stroller dock), unit supply price RMB 2,000, total price RMB 100,000, remarks: using a straight tube hanging method for storing children's strollers. In addition, it also purchased shared umbrella rental equipment (umbrella dock), umbrella handles, IoT cards, shared umbrella scan-to-borrow-and-return system software, and shared children's stroller scan-to-borrow-and-return system software. Product requirements: the appearance color and LOGO of the shared umbrella rental equipment (umbrella dock), umbrella handles, children's stroller rental equipment (stroller dock), and stroller handles provided by Party B must be sprayed according to the color and LOGO requirements provided by Party A. Party B is responsible for the design of the umbrella and children's stroller rental equipment, and Party A provides children's strollers to cooperate with Party B. Party B is responsible for the design and production of the children's stroller handle, and Party A provides children's stroller samples to cooperate with Party B. Total contract amount: RMB 145,650. Confidentiality agreement: Both parties undertake to keep confidential any documents and materials (including company plans, operational activities, technical information, and other trade secrets) belonging to the other party that are obtained during the discussion, signing, and execution of this contract and which cannot be obtained from public channels. Without the consent of the original provider of such materials and documents, neither party shall disclose all or part of the trade secrets to any third party. Party B has an absolute obligation of confidentiality regarding Party A's intellectual property rights, product materials, business model, and software functions related to the children's stroller rental equipment, and is prohibited from disseminating them in any form. Intellectual property: The design concepts, product design appearance, structure, system software functions, and business model related to the children's stroller rental equipment purchased by Party A under this contract are provided by Party A, and the intellectual property rights belong to Party A. Party B shall not apply for patents related to the children's stroller rental equipment.

On October 17, 2017, a WeChat chat record between "HuanXin-Cui Yuxin" and Fang Jiantao of FaRuiNa Company showed: on October 17, 2017, "HuanXin-Cui Yuxin" said: "Green is the umbrella dock specifications, yellow is the stroller dock specifications," and sent an image. FaRuiNa Company used this to support its claim that the October 27, 2017 Procurement Contract between the parties stipulated that the children's stroller rental equipment would use a straight tube hanging method, and the handle used would be a C-shaped handle rather than the mushroom head handle of the alleged infringing product in this case.

A WeChat group chat record titled "FaRuiNa-HuanXin Sharing... Supply Cooperation" showed: on October 30, 2017, "HuanXin-Zhou Weining" said: "@Fang Jiantao. FaRuiNa General Manager Fang, has the handle design started? When can you give us confirmation?" ... "FaRuiNa Wu Xiuwen - Commerce Department" said: "Since our structural engineer Brother Luo has received this task, he will certainly do his utmost to complete it." On November 1, 2017, "HuanXin-Cui Yuxin" said: "I have just communicated with General Manager Fang, the children's stroller handle will be designed by your side, and we will be responsible for subsequent mold opening and production." On November 3, 2017, "FaRuiNa Wu Xiuwen - Commerce Department" sent a design image and said: "This is the design drawing of the stroller handle." On November 3, 2017, "HuanXin Legal Representative Zhao Wei" said: "Technically, let's jointly carry out the structural modification of the handle; the current one won't work." On November 4, 2017, "HuanXin-Zhou Weining" said: "First, let him spend ten minutes drawing the shape on paper to see if his understanding is correct. This must be done; otherwise, it might be wrong when it comes out." "FaRuiNa Wu Xiuwen - Commerce Department" sent a design image. "HuanXin-Zhou Weining" said: "The shape is correct, move forward. Tell your engineer to keep the dimensions of the stroller pole consistent with the original stroller." On November 6, 2017, "HuanXin-Zhou Weining" said: "Is the specific design file ready?" "FaRuiNa Wu Xiuwen - Commerce Department" replied: "Come and take a look tomorrow." On November 7, 2017, "FaRuiNa Luo Guoyun" sent an image. On November 9, 2017, "HuanXin-Zhou Weining" said: "The money for purchasing the RFID tags has been transferred. I hope everyone helps to push forward fully." On November 10, 2017, "FaRuiNa Luo Guoyun" sent an image of the product prototype.

Faruina Company's delivery note No. FS2017111401 states: delivery date is November 14, 2017, receiving party is Huanxin Company, product names are pollen umbrella machine and umbrella handle. Faruina Company's delivery note No. FS2017121601 states: delivery date is December 16, 2017, receiving party is Huanxin Company, product name is one shared children's stroller, contract number 2017102601, remarks: complete accessories. Faruina Company's delivery note No. 2018012501 states: delivery date is January 25, 2018, receiving party is Huanxin Company, product name is one baby walking treasure. Faruina Company's delivery note No. FS2018020502 states: delivery date is February 5, 2018, receiving party is Huanxin Company, product name is 20 baby walking artifacts, contract number 2017102601, remarks: two units were sent on February 4. Faruina Company's delivery note No. FS2018031401 states: delivery date is March 14, 2018, receiving party is Huanxin Company, product name is children's stroller rental equipment (stake), contract number 2017102601. On May 8, 2018, Huanxin Company transferred RMB 35,500 to Faruina Company, remarks: down payment for Faruina shared children's stroller contract. On June 11, 2018, Huanxin Company transferred RMB 10,000 to Faruina Company, remarks: second batch procurement second installment (partial). On June 22, 2018, Huanxin Company transferred RMB 25,500 to Faruina Company, remarks: balance payment for Faruina's second batch procurement contract.

On December 5, 2017, an article published on Sohu.com titled "Functional Features of a Qualified Shared Baby Walking Artifact (Baby Walking Car)" recorded: the equipment is equipped with an embedded (RFID) electronic chip that records all information about the vehicle, including vehicle configuration, factory time, and the latest detailed rental record, enabling card-free return function.

The court of first instance held that: the patent in dispute is valid and should be protected by law. During the proceedings, upon comparison, the accused infringing product contains all the technical features of claim 1 of the patent in dispute, falling within the scope of protection of the patent in dispute. The main dispute in this case is whether the prior use defense and prior art defense raised by Faruina Company can be established.

(1) Regarding the prior use defense

Faruina Company claimed that before the filing date of the patent in dispute, it had already manufactured products identical to the patented technology and sold them to Bama Company and Daishujie Company. However, the contract submitted with Daishujie Company did not record the technical solution used in the products; the WeChat chat records contained corresponding design drawings, but without other supporting evidence, it is still difficult to directly determine based on this that the products actually delivered to the market under the contract used the patented technical solution. The contract signed with Bama Company on October 24, 2017, submitted by Faruina Company, did not disclose the technical solution used in the shared stroller equipment; the contract for work signed with Bama Company on February 1, 2018, recorded product design drawings, but only the front appearance design drawings, without fully disclosing the technical solution used. Even if the contract remarks indicated the provision of RFID sensing chips, it did not disclose the technical feature of the identification tag location. Secondly, even if under the contracts with Daishujie Company and Bama Company, Faruina Company manufactured and sold products identical to the patent in dispute, the evidence on record shows that the design drawings of the mushroom head handle in dispute were also formed during the performance of the Procurement Contract with Huanxin Company. Pursuant to the contract, Faruina Company had an absolute duty of confidentiality regarding Huanxin Company's children's stroller rental equipment intellectual property, product materials, business model, and software functions. Therefore, under the condition of breaching the contract, its claim of use under the contracts with Bama Company and Daishujie Company does not constitute prior use. Therefore, Faruina Company's prior use defense cannot be established.

(2) Regarding the prior art defense

Faruina Company submitted evidence showing that under the Procurement Contract, it delivered products using the accused infringing technical solution to Huanxin Company on three occasions: December 16, 2017, January 25, 2018, and February 4, 2018. Huanxin Company did not acknowledge this, arguing that only the appearance was similar. However, first, the WeChat chat records of the parties show that during the performance of this contract, the parties had already discussed in detail the technical solution related to the patent in dispute. The design drawings of November 7, 2017, and the actual product photographs of November 10, 2017, clearly reveal the technical features of the patent in dispute. Second, Huanxin Company acknowledged during the proceedings that the products delivered by Faruina Company were used in the automatic rental terminal system, and the delivery notes mentioned above clearly recorded the procurement contract number. Therefore, based on the comprehensive evidence, it can be determined that under the above delivery notes, Faruina Company delivered products using the accused infringing technical solution. In the absence of evidence that Faruina Company required Huanxin Company to take confidentiality measures regarding the products in transit, it can be presumed that the accused infringing technical solution was made public after the relevant products were delivered to the carrier for transport on February 4, 2018, and thus entered the market. Therefore, Faruina Company's prior art defense is established. Accordingly, Huanxin Company's claim that Faruina Company, Zhouzhuang Travel Company, and Zhenbian Company committed acts infringing the patent in dispute lacks legal basis.

The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 22, paragraph 5, Article 62, and Article 69, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2008) (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law), and Article 15, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, rendered the civil judgment (2019) Su 05 Min Chu No. 177 on June 24, 2020, with the following judgment: The claim of Shanghai Huanxin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. is dismissed. Court costs of first instance of RMB 9,009 are borne by Huanxin Company.

During the second instance, Huanxin Company submitted the following evidence to this Court:

Evidence 1: The Contract for Manufacturing Baby Walking Cart Handle Mold between Huanxin Company and a third party, Yongkang Hanchuang Mold Processing Factory (hereinafter referred to as Hanchuang Processing Factory), and the corresponding payment vouchers. The content is that Huanxin Company commissioned Hanchuang Processing Factory to manufacture a baby walking cart handle mold, with a contract amount of RMB 11,100, stipulating that Huanxin Company would provide 2D, 3D drawings and other relevant materials to Hanchuang Processing Factory, the contract would take effect upon signing by both parties, and the mold development period was 15 days. The date of execution is November 12, 2017. Payment vouchers show that Huanxin Company transferred RMB 5,500 and RMB 5,600 to Xu Yongda on November 15, 2017, and January 4, 2018, respectively, with the second payment voucher noted as "balance payment for mold."

Evidence 2: WeChat chat records. Huanxin Company claims that "Weining" in the chat records is an employee of Huanxin Company, and "Aa Ada (Hanchuang Plastic Mold Manufacturing)" is an employee of Hanchuang Processing Factory. On November 7, 2017, "Weining" sent to "Aa Ada (Hanchuang Plastic Mold Manufacturing)" pictures of the handle reflecting all the technical features of the patent in dispute.

The above Evidence 1 and 2 are intended to prove that Huanxin Company commissioned Hanchuang Processing Factory, a third party, to manufacture the baby walking cart handle mold. Therefore, the technical solution of the patent in dispute was not completed by Faruina Company, nor was it manufactured by Faruina Company. Faruina Company could not have delivered the patented product to Huanxin Company.

Evidence 3: The Baby Walking Cart Procurement and Renovation Service Contract between Huanxin Company and a third party, Yongkang Yiyuan Industry and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yiyuan Company), and the corresponding payment vouchers. The content is that Huanxin Company provided the baby walking cart handle mold, and Yiyuan Company would produce baby walking cart handles according to the mold and fit them to the baby walking cart push rods provided by Huanxin Company. It is intended to prove that Huanxin Company commissioned Yiyuan Company, a third party, to manufacture the patented product. Therefore, the technical solution of the patent in dispute was not developed by Faruina Company, nor did Faruina Company manufacture the baby walking cart handle; Faruina Company could not have delivered the patented product to Huanxin Company.

Evidence 4: WeChat chat records between Huanxin Company and the patent agency company, and corresponding pictures.

Evidence 5: The technical disclosure document for the patent in dispute sent by Huanxin Company to the patent agency company in the WeChat chat records.

The above Evidence 4 and 5 are intended to prove that the technical solution of the patent in dispute was formed during the discussions between Huanxin Company and the patent agency company, not developed by Faruina Company. Faruina Company could not have delivered the patented product to Huanxin Company.

Evidence 6: Civil judgments of the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court (2019) Yue 73 Zhi Min Chu No. 783, (2019) Yue 73 Zhi Min Chu No. 1211, and (2019) Yue 73 Zhi Min Chu No. 1212. Intended to prove that Faruina Company maliciously preempted patent applications during its cooperation with Huanxin Company, and after Huanxin Company filed a patent ownership dispute action, the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court has ruled that the patents preemptively applied for by Faruina Company in the three cases belong to Huanxin Company.

Evidence 7: Copy of the express waybill of Best Express and the waybill inquiry, chat records. Waybill number is 10695496033, sender is "Zhou", recipient is "Ma Qingyong", recipient address is "Ticket Office of Ferris Wheel Entertainment City, Hunan Road, Liaocheng, Shandong", item column records "shared umbrella rack", quantity "1 piece", packaging "wooden box". Inquiry records show that on February 4, 2018, the express item was sent from Shatou, Chang'an Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province, and was signed for on February 8. Intended to prove that the products delivered by Faruina Company to the carrier on February 4, 2018, did not include the patented product, but rather a shared umbrella rack, and the products were strictly packaged during transport, not constituting prior art.

Evidence 8: Web page printout from xuzhi.net. The web page shows that after logging into the xuzhi.net webpage (http://www.xuzhi.net/d198/15030620.html), only text is displayed, no pictures.

Evidence 9: Web page printout from 360 search results. The web page shows that after searching "shared baby walking cart" on 360, no articles or pictures from the xuzhi.net website as claimed by Faruina Company were found in the search results.

The above Evidence 8 and 9 are intended to prove that the article on the xuzhi.net website claimed by Faruina Company has no relevant pictures, does not disclose the accused infringing technical solution, and does not constitute prior art.

Evidence 10: The Invalidation Request Decision No. 47424 (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 47424) made by the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) on January 6, 2021. This decision was made in response to the invalidation request filed by Faruina Company regarding the patent in dispute. The decision records that during the invalidation procedure, the CNIPA organized both parties to demonstrate in court the posting and modification of content on the xuzhi.net website, and the CNIPA recognized the authenticity and publication date of the said website content, considering that this evidence can serve as prior art for evaluating the novelty of the patent in dispute. The decision found that: the technical solution claimed in claim 1 of the patent in dispute possesses novelty. Intended to prove that the validity of the patent in dispute is stable.

Faruina Company's opinion on cross-examination: The authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 1-5 are not recognized. Even if Huanxin Company commissioned a third party to manufacture the mold and handle, this does not prove that Faruina Company did not deliver products containing the patented technical solution, and cannot achieve its purpose of proof. The earliest time Faruina Company sent pictures showing the patented technical features to Huanxin Company was November 7, 2017, which is earlier than the time Huanxin Company commissioned the third party to make the mold. The evidence on record can indirectly prove that each delivery by Faruina Company included the accused infringing product. The authenticity of Evidence 6 is recognized, but the above judgments are not final judgments. Evidence 7 is not recognized as relevant to this case. The authenticity of Evidence 8-10 is recognized, but they cannot overturn the facts claimed by Faruina Company. Faruina Company has filed an administrative lawsuit against Decision No. 47424 of Evidence 10, and this decision is not yet final.

Zhenbian Company and Zhouzhuang Travel Company's opinion on cross-examination: The above evidence was formed before the judgment of first instance, does not constitute new evidence for the second instance, and lacks relevance to this case.

This Court's certification opinion: Based on the form of the evidence itself and combined with the opinions on cross-examination of Faruina Company, Zhenbian Company, and Zhouzhuang Travel Company, the authenticity of Evidence 1-10 is confirmed. Evidence 1-3, although they can prove that Huanxin Company commissioned a third party to manufacture the mold for the patented product and produce products based on the mold, these evidences are insufficient to negate the fact that Faruina Company, based on the contractual relationship between the parties, manufactured the patented product and mailed it to Huanxin Company. Therefore, Evidence 1-3 submitted by Huanxin Company are insufficient to achieve its purpose of proof. Regarding Evidence 4-5, the communication records between Huanxin Company and the patent agency and the technical disclosure document lack relevance to whether Faruina Company manufactured and mailed the patented product to Huanxin Company. Evidence 6 does not involve the patent in dispute and has no direct relevance to the infringement determination in this case. The information in Evidence 7 regarding the recipient, sender, and recipient address of the waybill lacks a direct corresponding relationship with the express delivered by Faruina Company to Huanxin Company on February 4, 2018, as found by the court of first instance, and is insufficient to achieve its purpose of proof. Although the webpage printouts of Evidence 8-9 do not display relevant pictures, the CNIPA conducted an on-site demonstration of the relevant webpage content during the invalidation procedure, and Faruina Company provided accordingly the response from xuzhi.net customer service on this issue, which is reasonably well-founded. Therefore, Evidence 8 and 9 submitted by Huanxin Company are insufficient to achieve their purpose of proof. Evidence 10 is an invalidation decision made by the CNIPA; its authenticity, legality, and purpose of proof are confirmed.

During the second instance, Faruina Company also submitted three pieces of evidence to this Court:

Counter-evidence 1: Notarization Document (2020) Yue Dong Wan Nan Hua No. 4872. On April 20, 2020, Faruina Company's representative Yang Xiaohui commissioned the Nanhua Notary Public Office of Dongguan City, Guangdong Province to notarize the browsing process of the xuzhi.net website (URL: http://www.xuzhi.net/d198/15030620.html). The notarized webpage shows the article title as "Shared Baby Walking Cart System, Chongzuo Shared Baby Walking Cart, Faruina Shared Baby Walking Cart", with publication time and entity displayed as: 2017-12-5 12:08:07, Guangdong Faruina Technology Co., Ltd. This article briefly reviews the development process of shared children's strollers and introduces the model of shared children's strollers and the situation of Faruina Company. The content of this evidence is the same as Evidence 1-1 in Decision No. 47424.

Counter-evidence 2: Notarization Document (2020) Yue Dong Wan Nan Hua No. 13799. On August 3, 2020, Faruina Company's representative Yang Xiaohui commissioned the Nanhua Notary Public Office of Dongguan City, Guangdong Province to search for "shared baby walking cart" on the www.so.com webpage. In the displayed search results, clicking on "Shared Baby Walking Cart System, Chongzuo Shared Baby Walking Cart, Faruina Shared Baby Walking Cart (xuzhi.net)" displayed the same page as Counter-evidence 1.

The above Counter-evidence 1 and 2 are intended to prove that the accused infringing technical solution was made known to the public through the internet before the filing date and constitutes prior art.

Counter-evidence 3: The Notice of Acceptance of Invalidation Request made by the CNIPA on May 6, 2020, deciding to accept the invalidation request concerning the patent in dispute. Intended to prove that the validity of the patent in dispute is unstable.

Huanxin Company's opinion on cross-examination: The above counter-evidence was submitted after the second instance trial. The authenticity and relevance of Counter-evidence 1 and 2 are not recognized. Upon webpage inquiry, the page displayed when browsing the relevant webpage shows only text, without pictures, so the possibility of forgery of the two pieces of evidence exists. Even if genuine, the pictures displayed on the webpage are plan views and do not disclose all technical features of the accused infringing technical solution. In particular, the components in the pictures have no textual descriptions, so a person of ordinary skill in the art, even upon seeing them, could not establish a one-to-one correspondence with the components of the accused infringing technical solution. Notably, Faruina Company has used this evidence as a comparison document to file an invalidation request, and Decision No. 47424 made by the CNIPA clearly found that Counter-evidence 1 and 2 did not disclose the technical solution of claim 1 of the patent in dispute. The authenticity of Counter-evidence 3 is recognized, but Decision No. 47424 has already maintained the validity of the patent in dispute.

Zhenbian Company and Zhouzhuang Travel Company's opinion on cross-examination: The authenticity and legality of the above evidence are recognized.

This Court's certification opinion: Counter-evidence 1 and 2 are notarization documents. In the absence of contrary evidence overturning the contents recorded in the notarization documents, this Court confirms the authenticity of the form and content of these evidences. Counter-evidence 3 is a document issued by the CNIPA; its authenticity and legality are confirmed. Whether the above evidence can achieve Faruina Company's purpose of proof will be comprehensively determined in light of the facts of the entire case.

The facts found by the court of first instance are basically true and are confirmed by this Court.

This Court additionally finds that the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court accepted on June 24, 2019, a dispute over the ownership of the utility model patent right with patent number ZL201820489897.2, titled "Shared Children's Stroller Stake," between Huanxin Company and Faruina Company, and ruled that the patent right belongs to Huanxin Company. On November 20, 2020, this Court rendered Civil Judgment (2020) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 1008 (hereinafter referred to as Judgment No. 1008), dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. That judgment found: "Based on the literal meaning of the intellectual property clauses in the contract in dispute, the relevant contractual clauses should be understood as that the patent rights to the children's stroller rental equipment and related designs involved in the contract belong to Huanxin Company." "Faruina Company has a duty of confidentiality regarding Huanxin Company's children's stroller rental equipment intellectual property, product materials, business model, and software functions."

It is further found that on May 7, 2018, Zhenbian Company (Party A) and Faruina Company (Party B) signed a Sales Contract No. 2018050701, stating: Party A purchases from Party B shared children's stroller equipment and children's stroller software programs. Among them, 50 units of shared children's stroller equipment are purchased at a unit price of RMB 3,500, total price RMB 175,000; one set of children's stroller software program is purchased at a unit price of RMB 20,000. On December 5, 2018, Faruina Company issued a confirmation letter to Zhenbian Company, stating: "It is hereby confirmed that the design patent products you purchased from our company -- shared children's stroller equipment (patent number: ZL201730601817.9), shared children's stroller handle (patent number: ZL201730603149.3), shared children's stroller stake (patent number: ZL201820489897.2), and shared baby walking cart time-sharing rental system V1.0 (computer software copyright registration certificate registration number: 2018SR436374) (specific purchase conditions shall be subject to the actual transaction between the parties) can be applied to the pollen shared children's stroller operated by your company. This confirmation letter is valid during the period when your company purchases the above design patent products from our company."

This is a dispute over infringement of invention patent. Because the accused infringing conduct occurred after October 1, 2009 and before June 1, 2021, the Patent Law as amended in 2008 shall apply to this case. In the opinion of this Court, based on the facts of this case and the allegations and defenses of the parties, the issues in dispute in the second instance are: whether the products delivered by Faruina for carriage included the accused infringing product; whether Faruina's prior art defense is sustainable; and the bearing of legal liability in this case.

1. Whether the products delivered by Faruina for carriage included the accused infringing product

Huanxin appealed, arguing that the only products it commissioned Faruina to manufacture were the child stroller storage devices (docking stations), and did not include the accused infringing product. Therefore, the products delivered by Faruina for carriage did not include the accused infringing product. In this regard, this Court holds that:

First, according to the facts found by the court of first instance, under the Procurement Contract signed between Faruina and Huanxin, the two parties conducted a detailed discussion on the technical solution of the handle involved in the patent at issue. On November 7 and 10, 2017, the parties sent respectively a design rendering of the child stroller and a photograph of the actual product in a WeChat work group. The photograph clearly revealed the accused infringing technical solution. Subsequently, Faruina delivered child stroller products to Huanxin on three separate occasions. The court of first instance accordingly found that Faruina had delivered to Huanxin products that used the accused infringing technical solution. Second, Exhibits 1-5 submitted by Huanxin in the second instance can only prove facts such as that Huanxin had commissioned a third party to manufacture the mold for the product covered by the patent at issue and to produce products using that mold, and that Huanxin had commissioned a patent agency to file the patent at issue. They cannot prove that the products delivered by Faruina for carriage did not include the accused infringing product. As for Exhibit 7 submitted by Huanxin in the second instance, although it records the item delivered for carriage as a "shared umbrella rack," the information on this shipping order does not correspond to the delivery notes found by the court of first instance and cannot prove that the products delivered by Faruina for carriage did not include the accused infringing product. Therefore, the aforementioned evidence submitted by Huanxin in the second instance is insufficient to overturn the facts found by the court of first instance. The evidence on record can prove that Faruina has delivered the accused infringing product to Huanxin in accordance with the contract between the parties. The relevant finding of the court of first instance is correct, and this Court affirms it. Huanxin's appeal on this issue is not supported by this Court.

2. Whether Faruina's prior art defense is sustainable

Article 62 of the Patent Law provides: "In a patent infringement dispute, if the alleged infringer has evidence to prove that the technology or design that it exploits is prior art or prior design, such exploitation shall not constitute patent infringement." Paragraph 5 of Article 22 provides: "For the purposes of this Law, 'prior art' means technology that is known to the public domestically or abroad before the date of filing of the patent application." It can be seen that the prerequisite for the establishment of prior art is that the technology was in the public domain before the filing date of the patent application at issue.

In this case, Faruina does not dispute that the accused infringing product includes all the technical features of claim 1 of the patent at issue and falls within the scope of protection of the patent at issue. Its main ground for its non-infringement defense is that the accused infringing product uses prior art, specifically two items: first, that the article and pictures published by Faruina on the Xuzhi Network caused the accused infringing technical solution to become known to the public; second, that Faruina's delivery of the child stroller rental equipment at issue for carriage caused the accused infringing technical solution to become known to the public.

(1) Whether the article and pictures published by Faruina on the Xuzhi Network caused the accused infringing technical solution to become known to the public

The system of prior art defense, on the one hand, can prevent the public from being disturbed by infringement lawsuits brought by patentees who have been improperly granted patents, providing a more convenient remedy outside the administrative procedure for invalidation. On the other hand, it also provides a stable and reasonable expectation for members of the public who use prior art in good faith, allowing them to reasonably predict and evaluate their own conduct. With respect to the former, a patent that has been improperly granted should obviously not receive legal protection, and the public may freely use that technology. With respect to the latter, regardless of whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent at issue, as long as the actor uses prior art, it can be used lawfully. Therefore, in general, any technology that was known to the public domestically or abroad before the date of filing (including, but not limited to, technology made public through publication or public use) can serve as the basis for the alleged infringer to raise a prior art defense.

However, civil subjects engaging in civil activities must follow the principle of good faith and must not violate the law or public order and good customs. This is a fundamental principle of civil law. As a defense in a civil action for infringement, the exercise of a prior art defense must also follow the above fundamental principles of civil law. The alleged infringer must be in good faith or without fault in relation to the defense. No one can benefit from their own illegal or improper conduct. If the prior art that the alleged infringer relies on for a prior art defense is a technical solution that was made public by the alleged infringer itself or by a third party at its instigation in violation of an express or implied confidentiality obligation, then the alleged infringer may not rely on that prior art to assert a prior art defense. Otherwise, the alleged infringer would benefit from its own illegal disclosure, which would clearly violate the fundamental principles of civil law and the legislative intent of the Patent Law.

In this case, pursuant to the Procurement Contract signed by Huanxin and Faruina on October 27, 2017, the patent rights to the child stroller rental equipment and related designs purchased by Huanxin belong to Huanxin, and Faruina has a confidentiality obligation with respect to the intellectual property, product materials, business model, and software functions of the child stroller rental equipment. Accordingly, Faruina's act of publishing the article and pictures on the Xuzhi Network constitutes a disclosure in breach of the contractual confidentiality obligation. Faruina disclosed the technical solution of the patent at issue without the consent of Huanxin, the patentee, thereby breaching its contractual obligations. Its conduct is illegal and blameworthy. Based on the aforementioned fundamental principles of civil law, it cannot rely on that prior art to assert a prior art defense. The counter-evidence submitted by Faruina in the second instance cannot be used to support its asserted prior art defense, and this Court does not support it.

(2) Whether Faruina's delivery of the child stroller rental equipment at issue for carriage caused the accused infringing technical solution to become known to the public

According to the principle that "he who asserts must prove," Faruina claims that the products it delivered for carriage caused the accused infringing technical solution to be made public. It should therefore bear the burden of proving that the delivery for carriage caused the accused infringing technical solution to be in a state where the public could access and learn its technical content. However, in this case, Faruina has no evidence to prove that the products it delivered for carriage were in a state where the public could access and learn their technical content.

First, Faruina, as the consignor, did not submit any evidence to prove the packaging state of the products at issue when they were delivered for carriage. That is, there is no evidence proving that the products it delivered for carriage were not sealed and were visible at any time. Nor did it prove that child stroller products are typically delivered for carriage without packaging or with transparent packaging. Therefore, the court of first instance's inference, based on the absence of evidence that Huanxin required Faruina to take confidentiality measures for the products during transportation, that the relevant products were in a public state is not only inconsistent with the rules of civil evidence but also lacks reasonableness.

Second, even if the products delivered by Faruina for carriage were not sealed, it cannot be concluded that they were in a state where the public could access and learn their technical content. Generally, only when a product enters the market for sale can it be presumed to be known to the public. Processes such as transportation and warehousing are generally relatively closed. During transportation, warehousing, and similar processes, the product is not in a state where the public can freely access or observe it, nor is it something the public can access or learn at will. As for the personnel responsible for transportation and warehousing, even if they have some contact with the products delivered for carriage or warehousing, or even have some understanding of the technical solution of the products involved, because they have a legal or contractual duty of custody and care over the products, they cannot be considered as members of the public under the Patent Law, unless there is contrary evidence proving that during this process, there were acts of external display or promotion directed at unspecified persons, making the product and its technical content public. In this case, the evidence provided by Faruina cannot prove that during the carriage process, the carrier personnel engaged in acts of external display or promotion directed at unspecified persons, thereby making the product at issue and its technical content accessible to the public.

Therefore, Faruina's delivery of the relevant products for carriage did not cause the accused infringing technical solution to become known to the public. The court of first instance's finding that the delivery of the relevant products to the carrier for transportation resulted in the accused infringing technical solution being made public because they entered the market is improper, and this Court corrects it.

In summary, neither of the two prior art defenses asserted by Faruina is sustainable. Huanxin's relevant appeal is sustained, and this Court supports it.

3. Bearing of legal liability

(1) Civil liability to be borne by Faruina

As discussed above, Faruina's act of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product infringed Huanxin's patent right at issue. Huanxin's request for Faruina to cease manufacturing the accused infringing product and to compensate for losses should be supported. However, the evidence on record cannot prove that Faruina engaged in other infringing acts such as using or offering to sell the accused infringing product. This Court does not support Huanxin's claim in this regard.

(2) Civil liability to be borne by Zhenbian and Zhouzhuang Tourism

First, the evidence on record cannot prove that Zhenbian engaged in infringing acts such as selling or offering to sell the accused infringing product. Therefore, this Court does not support Huanxin's claim that Zhenbian should cease selling and offering to sell the accused infringing product.

Second, the Sales Contract submitted by Zhenbian, signed between Zhenbian and Faruina, and the confirmation letter issued by Faruina to Zhenbian can prove that the accused infringing product used by Zhenbian originated from Faruina. At the same time, the content of the confirmation letter regarding the authorization of the design patent right further proves that Zhenbian has exercised reasonable care in this case and had no intent to infringe. Therefore, based on the evidence on record, Zhenbian's legal source defense has factual and legal basis. It may be exempted from civil liability for compensation for losses. Moreover, because it paid reasonable consideration, pursuant to Article 25 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, it is also not required to bear civil liability for ceasing use of the accused infringing product. Based on the same facts and reasoning, Zhouzhuang Tourism's legal source defense is also established. It is also not required to bear civil liability for ceasing use of the accused infringing product or for compensating for losses. This Court does not support Huanxin's corresponding claims.

(3) Economic losses and reasonable expenses

Article 65 of the Patent Law provides: "The amount of damages for patent infringement shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the patentee as a result of the infringement. If the actual losses are difficult to determine, the damages may be determined based on the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement. If both the losses of the patentee and the profits gained by the infringer are difficult to determine, the damages shall be reasonably determined by reference to a multiple of the patent licensing fee. The amount of damages shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the patentee to stop the infringement. If both the losses of the patentee and the profits gained by the infringer and the patent licensing fee are difficult to determine, the people's court may, based on factors such as the type of patent right, the nature of the infringing act, and the circumstances of the infringement, determine an amount of damages between RMB 10,000 and RMB 1,000,000."

In this case, the evidence on record cannot prove the actual losses suffered by Huanxin due to Faruina's infringement or Faruina's profits from the infringement. There is also no patent licensing fee available for reference. This Court will reasonably determine the amount of damages based on Huanxin's claims, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the type of the patent at issue, the nature of the accused infringing conduct, and the circumstances of the infringement. Specifically, this Court considers the following factors: 1. The type of the patent at issue is a utility model; 2. The accused infringing conduct occurred in a tourist scenic area with frequent personnel flow; 3. In the procurement contract signed between Faruina and Huanxin, the parties expressly stipulated the ownership of intellectual property rights and confidentiality obligations with respect to the child stroller rental equipment. Under these circumstances, Faruina still violated the fundamental principles of civil law and the contractual confidentiality obligations, made public on the internet pictures and information about the functions of the child stroller rental equipment at issue, and used this as evidence to assert a prior art defense. Taking the above factors into comprehensive consideration, this Court fully supports Huanxin's claim for economic losses of RMB 500,000.

With respect to reasonable expenses, the notarization fees and attorney fees incurred by Huanxin for this lawsuit are objectively present and supported by corresponding evidence. Therefore, this Court fully supports its reasonable expenses of RMB 20,904.3. Although the legal source defenses of Zhenbian and Zhouzhuang Tourism are established, a legal source defense is merely a defense against liability for damages, not a defense of non-infringement. The establishment of a legal source defense does not change the infringing nature of the act of using the accused infringing product. Since the reasonable expenses for rights protection are incurred based on the infringing act, even if the legal source defense is established, Zhenbian and Zhouzhuang Tourism must still bear joint and several liability with Faruina for the reasonable expenses paid by Huanxin for this lawsuit.

In summary, Huanxin's appeal is partially sustained. Pursuant to Article 22, paragraph 5, Article 62, Article 65, and Article 70 of the Patent Law of the PRC as amended in 2008, Article 25 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2019) Su 05 Min Chu No. 177 of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province, is reversed;

2. Guangdong Faruina Technology Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease its acts of infringing the utility model patent right with the patent number ZL 201820194071.3 and entitled "A connecting handle for use in an automatic rental terminal system," i.e., immediately cease manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product;

3. Guangdong Faruina Technology Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Shanghai Huanxin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. for economic losses of RMB 500,000 and reasonable expenses of RMB 20,904.3. Beijing Zhenbian Network Technology Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Shuixiang Zhouzhuang Tourism Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several liability for the part of RMB 20,904.3 in reasonable expenses;

4. The other claims of Shanghai Huanxin Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the delayed payment shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 9,009 and the second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 9,009 shall be borne by Guangdong Faruina Technology Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
